text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria has posted $335.1 million trade surplus for the first quarter of this year, National Statistics Institute figures showed.

-- The new Bulgarian National Bank seven-member board is expected to hold its first meeting today after the three board members, appointed by President Petar Stoyanov were sworn in on Sunday. Parliament elected the governor and his three deputies earlier last week.
-- Bulgaria launches today the third and final tender of its voucher privatisation programme, the Mass Privatisation Centre said.
Private investors and privatisation funds are expected to bid for 556 state firms with a total capital of 28.2 million levs. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to raise central heating charges by 25 percent from July, Energy Committee officials said.

-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov is leaving for an official visit in Kuwait today to promote investment opportunities in Bulgaria at a meeting with Kuwait's leader Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah.

-- Solvay Sodi JSCO, the Bulgarian unit of Belgium's chemical and pharmaceuptical group Solvay said it would invest some 40 billion levs in production and storage facilities at its soda ash plant plant in Devnya. @
-- Bulgaria's biggest state oil refinery Neftochim has posted some 33 billion lev loss last year, government officials said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
